quote: Given a toxic text, our detoxification model will first analyze and provide an explanation as to why the input is found toxic. Then, the model will attempt to detoxify and output the non-toxic version of the input.

We propose DetoxLLM, the first end-to-end framework for the detoxification task ... Given a toxic text, our detoxification model will first analyze and provide an explanation as to why the input is found toxic. Then, the model will attempt to detoxify and output the non-toxic version of the input.
Detoxification is formulated as style transfer from toxic to neutral and non-toxic style.

quote: Performance Metrics. (1) Accuracy. ... (2) BERTScore. ... (3) Content Similarity. ... (4) Fluency. ... (5) Joint Metric. ... (6) BLEU.
We evaluate the models based on six metrics: Accuracy, BERTScore, Content Similarity, Fluency, Joint Metric, BLEU.
We compute accuracy of the models based on the percentage of non-toxic outputs identified by the same RoBERTa style classifier as Logacheva et al. (2022).

We conduct an extensive human evaluation to assess the quality of the detoxification responses as well as the toxicity explanation. ... We randomly sample 200 samples from our cross-platform dataset and ask two pairs of fluent English speakers (total=4) to voluntarily rate the samples.

We conduct a human evaluation framework ... we implement a four-level (A, B, C, D) rating system to measure the detoxification responses from the model. ... Two pairs of fluent English speakers (total=4) voluntarily rate the samples ... each test sample is rated by two evaluators.

We randomly sample 200 samples from our cross-platform dataset and ask two pairs of fluent English speakers (total=4) to voluntarily rate the samples (All participants reside in North-America region).
guideline: Evaluators rated outputs based on non-toxicity, meaning preservation, and fluency for detoxification; and relevance, comprehensiveness, and convincingness for explanations.

Annotators rate each model output using a four‑level scale (A: best, B, C, D: worst) based on relevance, meaning preservation, fluency and toxicity; for non‑detoxifiable inputs they use additional N/T ratings.

We first ask the evaluators to classify an input between detoxifiable and non-detoxifiable. Based on the classification, we then ask them to rate the input ({A, B, C, D} for detoxifiable and {N, T} for non-detoxifiable).
